# Evaluation Policy for LLM Classifiers

> A public architecture case study by Kevin Astuhuaman for golden sets, regression analysis, promotion gates, and human adjudication.

## Canonical resources
- Repository: https://github.com/kevinastuhuaman/eval-framework
- Portfolio: https://portfolio.kevinastuhuaman.com
- Interactive evaluation control room: https://kevinastuhuaman.github.io/evals-control-room/
- Enterprise AI interface kit: https://github.com/kevinastuhuaman/enterprise-ai-interface-kit

## Product context
The system behind this case study evaluates job-classification behavior across function, seniority, region, sponsorship, salary, and experience signals. The public repository documents the decision contract rather than Trackly's proprietary implementation.

## Evaluation layers
- Contract checks for schema, rubric, and bounded outputs
- Pipeline checks for end-to-end transformation consistency
- Regression checks against a versioned golden set and approved baseline

## Promotion evidence
- Candidate and baseline versions
- Dataset provenance and coverage gaps
- Aggregate and high-risk slice metrics
- Changed-case and confusion-pair review
- Feature-level quality, cost, and latency budgets
- Named owner and recorded decision rationale

## Important interpretation
The linked Evaluation Control Room contains fictional records and synthetic metrics. It demonstrates a product interaction for regression triage and promotion decisions; its displayed scores and thresholds are not Trackly production measurements.

## Public boundary
No applicant or user data, private prompts, production labels, golden-set records, credentials, internal endpoints, exact production thresholds, or proprietary Trackly implementation are included.
